findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently overrides the 5-arg version
findings.body: Ruby has no overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Any existing caller using the width/height form now passes `max_height` as `opts`. That either raises (for example when `opts[:allow_animation]` is called on an Integer) or silently drops the options. The earlier definition at line 145 is dead code. Remove one of the two, or have a single method that accepts either form.

findings.title: Downsize loop overwrites the tempfile in place, with no failure check and a wrong extension
findings.body: The result of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If convert fails, the loop retries the same unchanged file five times with no feedback. The tempfile is also overwritten in place, so `tempfile.size` may be stale if the File object caches it. The controller does not update `content_type` or `filename` to match the converted output. For animated GIFs, `optimize` only picks the animated path when the path matches `/\.GIF$/i`. Tempfile paths from uploads often lack an extension, so `convert` may fail or choose the wrong output format. The `"80%"` resize also ends up in `downsize_instructions` as `-resize 80%\>`. That form only shrinks if the image is larger than 80% of itself, which is always true, but it behaves oddly with `force_aspect_ratio`.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB and ignores site settings
findings.body: The client now ignores `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`, replacing them with a fixed 10MB. Attachments, which are not downsized, can now pass client validation, hit the server limit, and get a generic error. The same applies to the 413 handler. The error message now reports 10MB even when the real limit is different. The server-side `10.megabytes` in the API URL download is likewise a hard-coded value that no longer follows the site setting. A shared constant or the settings should be used instead.

findings.title: API URL download limit no longer tied to site settings
findings.body: `FileHelper.download` was previously limited by `max_image_size_kb`. It is now fixed at 10MB regardless of the setting, and the oversized-image reduction only runs for images. Non-image files fetched through the API are therefore allowed up to 10MB, bypassing the configured attachment limit at this stage.
